marta-cs: FYI — ACME reported spikes of 429s this morning even though their app only shows ~60 req/min across several projects. They pasted a sample error: `{'error':'quota_exhausted','scope':null}`
lia-support: Can you grab the response headers and the raw Authorization header they used? Also do they go through a customer proxy/NAT?
marta-cs: Customer says they use an internal proxy that forwards a single API key for multiple smaller projects. They are in us-east and mention an egress NAT. Sample from them:
```
status: 429
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 164s
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","scope":"unknown"}
```
lia-support: Ok — that setup can cause attribution ambiguity. @sam-eng can you check how our quota attribution heuristics look when a proxy strips org/project headers?
sam-eng: quick note: our attribution prefers (1) API key -> project, (2) org header, (3) client IP fallback. If the proxy reuses one key for many projects and strips identity headers, we fall back to the NAT IP which aggregates traffic. That will surface as a single bucket hitting limits.
tony-sre: +1. I've seen this exact pattern before. NATed egress + shared key -> burst from multiple tenants exhausts the IP-scoped or fallback bucket. Also possible that some internal retry loop amplifies load.
lia-support: Can we get the gateway logs for that customer's NAT IP and the auth logs for the API key? Also ask customer to run a quick repro with verbose curl to show `Remote-Addr` and response headers. Example repro command to ask them to run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
marta-cs: They ran 10 concurrent requests and observed 2x 429s. Attached the headers from one of the 429 responses above. They don't have per-project keys right now — everything routes through their proxy.
sam-eng: I queried logs for that API key and saw spikes from multiple internal project names between 08:15-08:18. We should also search for other projects using that key (likely misconfigured). Query: `index=gateway auth.key=<KEY> | stats count by src_ip,project`
tony-sre: Mitigations we can offer customers: (a) create per-project API keys (best), (b) configure proxy to forward org/project identity header instead of reusing a single key, (c) request a temporary quota bump for the customer's NAT IP range or assign a quota override for that key while they re-architect, (d) enable per-key burst allowance if feasible. For internal ops: open a quota-team ticket to evaluate NAT-range overrides and update our docs about attribution fallbacks.
lia-support: I'll send these suggestions to the customer and ask for the curl output and gateway logs. I will also open an internal ticket to quota-team with the logs and sam's query. Ticket: Q-1234.
deploy-bot: Alert created for 429 surge — id=alert-7832; target=quota-team
liа-support: (typo: lia-support) sending note now to customer, will update thread once I have the verbose curl output. :white_check_mark:
